content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Dallas

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires either a four-year degree plus three years of project-management experience, or a high-school diploma plus five years of equivalent experience. Review PMI's education and experience criteria now to verify you meet the baseline. Granite PM Academy staff can clarify eligibility questions before you enroll.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Instruction
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual PMP Bootcamp, delivered by active certified practitioners. Attend synchronous instructor-led sessions on a schedule that fits your work commitments across Banking and Financial Services, Telecommunications, Healthcare, Transportation and Logistics, Construction, or Energy sectors. You'll earn the 35 PMI-required contact hours upon completion.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After finishing the bootcamp, submit your official PMP application directly to PMI, including proof of your education, work experience, and 35 contact hours. Pay the PMI exam fee when you apply. Granite PM Academy provides guidance on the submission process and documentation requirements.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Pass the PMP Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice exams, study guides, and instructor Q&A sessions—to reinforce bootcamp content. Schedule your exam with Pearson VUE at a test center near Dallas. Sit for the computer-based exam and demonstrate mastery of project-management domains and processes.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP® Credential
steps_items.text: Your PMP® credential is valid for three years. Maintain it by earning Professional Development Units (PDUs) through training, certifications, volunteer work, or community service. Plan your PDU activities throughout the renewal cycle to stay current and demonstrate ongoing commitment to project-management excellence.
